properties.digitized_from: DataSF Assessor parcels (acdm-wktn): the east arm of lot 4232011 (recorded 2022-08-30; active), cut from the rest of that lot along a straight line, and all of lot 4232013 (recorded 2022-08-30; active). Cross-checked against Potrero Power Station Design for Development Figure 4.25.1 - Power Station Park and Louisiana Paseo: Concept Plan Overview (printed p.119), which labels the two park areas 'Power Station Park West' (2) and 'Power Station Park East' (1), and Figure 6.2.3 - Building Height Plan (printed p.245, PDF p.247).
properties.digitization_method: Traced from the Potrero Power Station Design for Development's own Figure 6.2.3 (Building Height Plan, p.245), which labels this feature directly (not inferred). Georeferenced using an affine transform fit from 8 control points -- the 4 real-world corners of Block 1 and the 4 real-world corners of Block 12 (both already independently traced and committed elsewhere in this dataset), matched to their pixel positions in this same diagram. Residual error against those 8 control points is roughly 15-24m, consistent with this site's other entries. This is a DIFFERENT (but equivalent-precision) point set than the 9 street-intersection points used for Blocks 1-15 -- both were derived from the same source diagram. CORRECTED 2026-09-16: user-flagged visual check found this polygon crossing back and forth over the same real paved road (Maryland Street) identified and fixed on Potrero Power Station Block 3 (see that file's digitization_method for the full curb-finding method) -- a thin north-south finger of this polygon ran right down the middle of the road next to the site office building, and the polygon's southern boundary crossed the road again further south. FIRST PASS (superseded): measured this stretch's own west and east curb points independently (two points per curb, 47m apart) and derived each curb's own bearing from its own two points -- produced curbs 1.7 degrees off-parallel from each other. SECOND PASS (superseded): reused Block 3's own directly-measured curb bearing (168.9 deg), reasoning it was the same physical street. THIRD PASS: user re-flagged the result as still not parallel to the road. Root cause found: Block 3's own 168.9 deg bearing (from the SECOND PASS) was itself wrong -- derived from only a 45m baseline, it violates this project's own bearing_trace.py guidance against narrow-baseline bearings. Checked it against three independent long-baseline references that all agreed with each other within 1 degree: the real OSM Maryland Street geometry itself (already sitting unused in data/raw/streets.geojson, bearing ~355 deg over multiple segments spanning both Block 3's and this polygon's latitude ranges, and ~355.3 deg over its full 220m length), and Pier 70's already-validated site grid bearing (356.5 deg, SITE_BEARINGS in bearing_trace.py) -- both point to ~356 deg, not 168.9/348.9 deg, a real 7-degree miss that the project's own check_bearing_sane() helper would have flagged immediately had it been run. Rebuilt the ribbon using 356.5 deg (this project's established Potrero/Pier 70 grid bearing) through the same directly-measured curb points from the second pass, extended 80m past them, and re-subtracted from the ORIGINAL (pre-any-clip) polygon via shapely's difference() -- removed about 20% of the polygon's area. Lesson for this dataset: added 'potrero': 356.5 to SITE_BEARINGS in bearing_trace.py so future bearing measurements at this site get sanity-checked automatically instead of relying on a fresh, possibly narrow-baseline read. FOURTH PASS: user pointed out the polygon's north and south caps (the two short segments connecting the new street-edge cut back to the rest of the park, next to the site office building and near the bottom of the L-shape) weren't perpendicular to the street -- both were leftover from the original diagram transform and had never been touched by any of the street-crossing passes above. Measured: north cap ran at 80.8 deg, south cap at 260.8 deg, both off by 5.7 deg from the correct perpendicular (86.5/266.5, i.e. 90 deg off the established 356.5 deg grid). Fixed by keeping the street-edge (ribbon-cut) endpoint of each cap fixed and rotating the other endpoint onto the perpendicular bearing, preserving each segment's original length (a 2.6-3.7m shift) -- a targeted local correction rather than a global re-trace, since only these two segments were flagged and the rest of the polygon's shape (against Blocks 7/8/9/11/12) has not been independently re-verified. REBUILT 2026-09-16: user-flagged that the diagram shows this park sharing sides directly with Blocks 7 and 11 (and, per the same diagram crop, 8 and 12 too), with zero gap -- this polygon's prior boundary (itself a MultiPolygon that had accumulated ~200 vertices across four rounds of street-crossing/perpendicularity patches) sat 5-21m away from Blocks 8/11/12 after those blocks were re-measured in the 2026-09-16 pixel pass, since this park file was never touched in that pass. A fresh pixel check of the diagram (crop of the Block 7/8/11/12/park area) confirmed the park is one simple contiguous rectangle bounded exactly by those four blocks -- Maryland Street does not continue south of Humboldt's row into this space in the plan. Replaced the whole accumulated shape with a clean quadrilateral built directly from Block 7's SW corner, Block 8's SE corner, Block 12's NE corner, and Block 11's NW corner (the exact, already-committed coordinates from those four files' own 2026-09-16 re-measurement), so the park now shares an exact vertex with each of the four blocks by construction rather than by a separate, error-prone measurement. This drops the old file's hard-won manual fix for a real paved road (Maryland Street, or a site access road) that currently physically cuts through part of this still-undeveloped area -- rather than re-deriving that by hand again, this now relies on this project's own standard src/join_approximate.py street-clipping step (already applied to every approximate polygon in this dataset) to automatically cut out any real, currently-mapped street from the published layer. The org's own build log should show the resulting clipped percentage. REFINED 2026-09-16 (same day, second pass): the first rebuild (4-corner quadrilateral) created small (20-40 m2) slivers of overlap with Block 7 and Block 8, because a straight line from Block 7's SW corner to Block 8's SE corner cuts across the small real jog between those two blocks' own bottom edges rather than following them. Switched to an 8-vertex polygon that walks Block 7's own SW-to-SE edge, then Block 8's own SW-to-SE edge, then down to Block 12's NE-to-NW edge, then Block 11's own NE-to-NW edge, and back -- using only coordinates already committed in those 4 blocks' own files, so the park's boundary now coincides exactly with each block's real edge with zero overlap and zero gap by construction. REFINED 2026-09-16 (same day, second pass): the first rebuild (4-corner quadrilateral) created small (20-40 m2) slivers of overlap with Block 7 and Block 8, because a straight line from Block 7's SW corner to Block 8's SE corner cuts across the small real jog between those two blocks' own bottom edges rather than following them. Switched to an 8-vertex polygon that walks Block 7's own SW-to-SE edge, then Block 8's own SW-to-SE edge, then down to Block 12's NE-to-NW edge, then Block 11's own NE-to-NW edge, and back -- using only coordinates already committed in those 4 blocks' own files, so the park's boundary now coincides exactly with each block's real edge with zero overlap and zero gap by construction. SPLIT 2026-09-16 (sixth pass): user pointed out this park's east edge (the 7/11 side) was eating into the real street corridor instead of stopping at Block 7/11's own edge, and that the park should continue as a SEPARATE piece east of that street, between Block 8 and Block 12. Checked data/raw/streets.geojson directly: Maryland Street's real OSM geometry does continue south through this exact area (down to lat 37.6557, spanning the full Block 11/12 row), confirming a real street genuinely separates the two halves -- this wasn't just an over-generous single rectangle. Also found and fixed the real bug that had been silently hiding this: src/join_approximate.py's automatic street-clipping discarded whichever fragment was smaller when a street split a polygon into two pieces, assuming any second piece was a tiny corner sliver -- here it was throwing away roughly half the park's real area (the whole Block 8/12 side). Fixed that function to keep any fragment at least 5% of the largest one, and rebuilt this feature from scratch as a MultiPolygon with two parts, each built directly from its own pair of blocks' own already-committed corners (Block 7's SW/SE + Block 11's NW/NE for the west part; Block 8's SW/SE + Block 12's NW/NE for the east part) -- so each part's edges are exact against its own blocks, with no encroachment into Maryland Street between them. 2026-09-29 accuracy audit: the source_doc_urls entry pointed to the August 22, 2019 public-review draft #2 of the Design for Development (potrero_power_D4D_draft-082219.pdf), which now returns 404 and has no archive snapshot; it has been repointed to the adopted final D4D (February 26, 2020, https://sfplanning.org/sites/default/files/documents/citywide/potreropower_D4D_final.pdf), where Figure 6.2.3 Building Height Plan is on printed p.245 (PDF p.247) and Table 3.1.1 Permitted Uses on printed p.47, and whose footers carry the February 26, 2020 date; the SF Planning project page (https://sfplanning.org/potrero-power-station) is added as the source for status and phasing. The 'REBUILT pass' entry above says the diagram confirmed the park is one simple contiguous rectangle bounded exactly by four blocks and that Maryland Street does not continue south of Humboldt's row into this space; the final D4D's Figure 6.2.3, viewed as a rendered image, contradicts that reading: Maryland Street is drawn continuing south from Humboldt Street to 23rd Street, 'POWER STATION PARK' is labelled only on the green rectangle between Blocks 7 and 11, an unlabelled green rectangle lies between Blocks 8 and 12, Block 9 is separate (east of Delaware Street), and 'LOUISIANA PASEO' runs between Block 15 and Blocks 7/11. (The later SPLIT entry above already reversed the reading, using OpenStreetMap.) Likewise the accuracy_caveat's earlier description of an 'irregular, non-rectangular shape woven between Blocks 7, 8, 9, 11, and 12' did not match the final figure and has been corrected in place. 2026-10-02: public-text pass. accuracy_caveat, why_no_real_parcel, notes reworded for readers (meaning unchanged; no change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type); previous wording -- accuracy_caveat: 'APPROXIMATE -- Figure 6.2.3 labels this open space directly but draws it in the final D4D as two plain green rectangles (the one between Blocks 7 and 11 is labelled 'POWER STATION PARK'; an unlabelled one lies between Blocks 8 and 12; Maryland Street runs between them and Block 9 is separate, east of Delaware Street); this is a two-part rectangular approximation (split 2026-09-16 by the real Maryland Street corridor that separates the Block 7/11 side from the Block 8/12 side -- see digitization_method), a trace of the diagram's rectangles. Each part shares an exact edge with its own two blocks by construction, so accuracy tracks whatever those block files carry.'; why_no_real_parcel: 'Open space with no subdivided Assessor parcel of its own within the largely unaddressed former power-station site. (This is our own parcel-search narration, not something the cited Design for Development can establish; the D4D does not address Assessor parcels.)'; notes: 'Simplified two-part rectangular approximation of a labeled open space (drawn in the final D4D as two rectangles) -- see accuracy_caveat.'. TRIMMED 2026-10-10 (overlap with a neighbour's Assessor lot; nothing else changed): Blocks 11 and 12 now use recorded Assessor lot lines (lots 4232021 and 4232023) as their outline, and this traced shape overlapped them by about 831 m2, so that area was cut from it (recorded lot lines win over a trace). Area 5,494 -> 4,663 m2, both parts kept. The earlier sign-off covered the traced shape; this trim was made at the owner's direction. REPLACED 2026-10-10 (shape; status and use unchanged): the owner read Assessor lots 4232011 and 4232012 as Louisiana Paseo and Power Station Park together, with 4232011 split between the paseo strip (continuing lot 4232012) and the park arm at right angles to it. The recorded east-edge vertices of both lots lie within 0.1 m of one straight line, which is used as the cut through 4232011 (about 33 m, not a recorded lot line). The outline is now the east arm of lot 4232011 (2,466 m2), in place of the earlier 4,663 m2 shape. geometry_type stays 'approximate' because of the cut. The final D4D draws the park as two green rectangles; the second, unlabelled one (between Blocks 8 and 12) has no matching lot and is not drawn here. The earlier sign-off covered the earlier shape; this change was made at the owner's direction. ADDED 2026-10-11 (second part; status, use and the first part unchanged): the 2026-10-10 REPLACED entry above said the D4D's second park rectangle, between Blocks 8 and 12, 'has no matching lot' and left it out. That was wrong. Active Assessor lot 4232013 (zoning PPS-MU, recorded 2022-08-30, added to the map 2023-12-01, no drop date; DataSF acdm-wktn queried 2026-10-11) lies under it: the earlier two-part rectangle's east part was 2,329 m2, of which 2,299 m2 (98.7%) was inside the lot, and it covered 90.7% of the lot (2,547 m2). Figure 4.25.1 (D4D p.119, 'Power Station Park and Louisiana Paseo: Concept Plan Overview') labels this area '1 Power Station Park East' and the area between Blocks 7 and 11 '2 Power Station Park West'; Figure 6.2.3 (p.245) draws it as unlabelled open space between Blocks 8 and 12. The outline now has two parts: the first as before, and all of lot 4232013, drawn from the Assessor's own lot lines with no cut. The lot shares its full north and south edges (about 74 m each) with lots 4232022 (Block 8) and 4232023 (Block 12) with no overlap (under 1 m2) and no gap, and lies about 19.5 m from the west part across Maryland Street. Area 2,466 -> 5,012 m2. Also corrected in the same pass: digitized_from named lot 4232012, but the park contains none of it (it is part of Louisiana Paseo). The earlier sign-off covered the earlier shape; this addition follows the owner's confirmation that lot 4232013 is the park that was dropped. 2026-10-11: text only. Public text that said the lots were 'assigned by the owner' now says they are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams, because readers would take 'owner' to mean the landowner. No change to the shape, status, use or geometry_type.
properties.accuracy_caveat: APPROXIMATE -- the outline is built from recorded Assessor lot lines except one cut. West part (between Blocks 7 and 11): the east arm of lot 4232011. The two lots 4232011 and 4232012 are Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams: Louisiana Paseo is the north-south strip made of lot 4232012 and the west strip of lot 4232011, and Power Station Park West is the east-west arm of lot 4232011. The line between them, about 33 m long through lot 4232011, is not a recorded lot line: it is the straight extension of the strip's east edge, which the recorded vertices of both lots lie on to within 0.1 m. East part (between Blocks 8 and 12): all of lot 4232013, a recorded lot, with no cut. No document names the lot as the park; it is matched by location to the D4D's Power Station Park East. The park is planned and not yet built.
properties.why_no_real_parcel: The park is two areas on two sets of lots: the west part is the east arm of Assessor lot 4232011 (assigned from Pier & Point's reading of the plan diagrams; its west edge is a straight extension, not a recorded lot line) and the east part is all of lot 4232013. Both lots are active, recorded 2022-08-30. No document names either lot as the park.
properties.regulatory_context: The site's central public open space, per the D4D's own Figure 6.2.3 label -- two rectangles, one between Blocks 7 and 11 (labelled 'POWER STATION PARK') and one between Blocks 8 and 12, on either side of Maryland Street; Block 9 lies east of Delaware Street and does not border it. Not yet built: consistent with the 2024 annual compliance report (March 2025) and the SF Chronicle of Aug 3, 2026 (Block 8 construction 'expected to begin in the fall'). Of the blocks around it, Block 7B (the Sophie Maxwell Building) sits 'between Humboldt Street, Maryland Street, Louisiana Paseo and Power Station Park' (2024 annual compliance report) and opened in October 2025 (SF YIMBY, Oct 24, 2025); the others are still planned.
properties.notes: Power Station Park of the Potrero Power Station Design for Development: West (between Blocks 7 and 11, on part of Assessor lot 4232011) and East (between Blocks 8 and 12, on Assessor lot 4232013).
